transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm here today because I've been struggling with really distressing memories and nightmares about a traumatic event that happened to me. It's been going on for about seven months now, and I just can't get them out of my head.
Have you found yourself actively trying to avoid thoughts, feelings, conversations, or places that remind you of this traumatic event?

Yes, I absolutely do. I try my best to block out any thoughts or feelings about it, and I completely avoid certain places and people that might remind me of what happened. It is just so exhausting to constantly push everything away like this.
Since the event, have you felt constantly on guard, easily startled, or had trouble sleeping or concentrating?

Yes, my sleep has been terrible—I struggle to fall asleep, wake up constantly from nightmares, and wake up too early feeling completely unrefreshed. I also feel constantly tense, anxious, and on guard all the time since it happened.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ['Posttraumatic Stress Disorder', 'Adjustment Disorder']. Based on the patient's report of persistent intrusive memories, nightmares, avoidance behavior, and hyperarousal symptoms (difficulty sleeping, being constantly on guard) lasting for seven months following a traumatic event, the criteria for Posttraumatic Stress Disorder are fully met. Adjustment Disorder is ruled out because the symptom presentation and duration align specifically with PTSD. No further questioning is needed.
